ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left of the figure is H3N, with one pair of lone-pair electron dots on nitrogen, and there is a curved arrow pointing to the middle carbon; the middle carbon is connected to R1 and R2, and forms a C=O double bond with the oxygen on the right; there is another curved arrow from the carbonyl region pointing to the right. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, ignore the curved arrows and the lone-pair electron dots on nitrogen, and also exclude all bonds involving hydrogen. Therefore N-H bonds are not counted, and the arrow from nitrogen to carbon is not treated as a bond. The non-hydrogen bond connections that actually need to be counted are: C-R1 single bond, C-R2 single bond, and C=O double bond. The total is 3 bonds.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Inspect the image first and list only actual bond connections that do not involve hydrogen. Ignore the two curved arrows and the nitrogen lone-pair dots. Count the C-R1 single bond, the C-R2 single bond, and the C=O double bond. Do not count any N-H bonds or the arrow from nitrogen to carbon. Total the listed non-hydrogen bond connections.

A double bond is one bond connection of type double for this count, not two separate counted connections. Bonds involving hydrogen, such as N-H in H3N, are excluded.

method.method_draft: After reading the image, form a non-hydrogen connectivity graph. Add an edge for each actual bond shown between non-hydrogen nodes: central C-R1, central C-R2, and central C-O. Leave out N-H edges because hydrogen is excluded, and leave out N-to-C because the image shows an arrow rather than a bond. Count the unique graph edges to obtain the total number of non-hydrogen bonds.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This uses a graph/adjacency interpretation rather than visual line tallying: convert the drawing into a heavy-atom connectivity graph and count unique edges.
planner_metadata.image_role: Identify the heavy/non-hydrogen nodes visible in the drawing: N from H3N, the carbonyl carbon at the center, O on the right, and substituent groups R1 and R2. From the drawn bond lines, the central carbon is connected to R1, R2, and O; nitrogen is not connected by a drawn bond, only by a curved arrow.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to define the target as the total number of bonds in the displayed transition-state structure, with arrows ignored and hydrogen-involving bonds excluded.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: A chemical structure can be represented as a graph whose nodes are non-hydrogen atoms or substituent groups and whose edges are bonds. Curved arrows and lone-pair dots are annotations, not graph edges. Unique heavy-atom edges are counted once regardless of whether the edge is single or double.
